dissented.on: the evidence entry for scripts/tests/test_sov_snapshot.py, that it fails when any number anywhere on the page is neither checked by a claim nor classified with a reason in the section it was ruled in
dissented.finding: Overclaimed. The TOKEN regex requires digits, then whitespace, then a letter, with a lookbehind excluding word characters, dot, slash and hyphen. Ten counts were planted one line above the Sov profile bullet in the live snapshot section and eight escaped with no finding at all: 77 before a period, 77 alone in a markdown table cell, 77 before a comma, 77 in parentheses, 77 before a backticked term, 77 before a dash, 77-surface hyphenated, and 3/77 after a slash. Only a bare 77 widgets and a count wrapped across a line were caught. The page's own house style puts numbers in tables and before backticked terms, so these are not exotic shapes. what_could_defeat_it names the fenced-block gap, the indented-block gap and the wrong-reason gap; it does not name this one.

residuals.finding: The check has no single referent for the record. Nine of ten claims are derived from working-tree filesystem state, which counts untracked files; commits is derived from committed history. A page that is true about the repository is therefore reported as drifted whenever any session holds untracked work under .claude/skills, .claude/workflows, decisions/, reports/ or services/. This witness watched it happen: at F1 the check was red with page says 21, record holds 22 and page says 19, record holds 20, purely because a sibling session was mid-creation of an unrelated skill. Applying the concern's own files to a clean tree at f89b4f0 reproduced a red landing deterministically. The consequence is not only a noisy gate. The sibling concern's own commit message records that it edited CLAUDE.md because the orientation snapshot check demanded it within a minute of the skill appearing. The gate exports an edit to a grant-excluded governing document into every unrelated concern that adds a skill, workflow, decision, report, service or check.

Two consequential refusals have no test. A grep for MIN_CHECKABLE, MAX_TOLERANCE and tolerance across scripts/tests/test_sov_snapshot.py returns nothing. Both were exercised by hand here and both fire correctly, but AGENTS.md requires a positive case and a case proving the refusal for every consequential behavior, and neither has either. The boundary is worth stating too: MIN_CHECKABLE of 0.5 against ten claims means exactly five underivable claims still prints PASS. The comment above the constant still describes a five-claim table, a gate that goes green having checked one claim in five, four of five is the CI shape, which is stale prose inside the module whose subject is stale prose.

The two floors disagree. cmd_check refuses below half the claims; selfcheck.run() refuses only at zero and will print PASS: 1 of 10 claims exercised, 7 cases. Running selfcheck alone on a degraded tree reports green having exercised a tenth of the table. cmd_check's own floor covers the composite, so this is a reporting defect rather than a hole, and the packet's wording, refuses rather than passing when it derived nothing, is literally accurate.

.claude/README.md, corrected in this concern from eighteen to nineteen executable workflows, is already wrong: 20 sov-*.js workflows are on disk and committed. The packet's residual 2 predicted this would go stale again tomorrow; it went stale within the hour, before landing. It is a live instance of that residual rather than a new class of problem.

on_accept under-enumerates what sits outside the grant. It names CLAUDE.md and LESSONS.md. STATUS.yaml, which the declared artifact list includes for queuing A5, is in excluded_paths, and acceptance/A5.json itself matches none of the admitted prefixes. The evidence entry for the grant names reports/ and LESSONS.md but not STATUS.yaml or acceptance/.

The artifact was not frozen for witnessing. acceptance/A5.json, CLAUDE.md and scripts/tests/test_sov_snapshot.py all changed bytes between the first and second reading of this witness, and CLAUDE.md was then committed by a third party. One test run taken mid-edit produced TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got tuple out of re.finditer, which was the transient state in which _prose_only had been changed to return a tuple and its caller had not yet been updated. That is explained and resolved and is not a defect in the presented bytes, but it means no reading of this artifact is a reading of a stable thing, and a witness's digests over an unfrozen tree are decorative.

Land the concern whole is not safe to execute literally in this tree. At F3 the working tree also carries .claude/epic/tree.json, four files under diagrams/, scripts/sovkernel/scope.py and scripts/tests/test_sov_land.py, all modified by other concerns. A whole-tree commit would sweep them.

The check reads numbers only, and this witness confirms the blindness is real rather than merely declared. The snapshot section names eight services in prose (Asset, Record, Console, Gateway, Observation, Proofing, Projection, Registry) while services/ holds ten; host and identity are counted by the number beside that sentence and named nowhere. The count is checked and correct, the sentence is incomplete, and the gate is silent. what_could_defeat_it item 3 covers this class honestly.

standing_supported.subject: scripts/sov_snapshot.py, scripts/sovsnapshot/, scripts/tests/test_sov_snapshot.py, and the orientation snapshot entry in scripts/sovverify/checks.py
standing_supported.note: Supported for the gate as built. Not supported for the packet's authority conclusion, which W2 disputes. This observation settles nothing and ratifies nothing.

judgement_items: Is a gate whose nine filesystem claims count untracked files the gate you want, given that it made an unrelated concern edit CLAUDE.md, a path the ratified standing grant excludes, within a minute of that concern adding one skill? The alternatives are all cheap: derive from git ls-files, widen the tolerance on the volatile counts, or accept that adding any skill, workflow, decision or report is now also a CLAUDE.md edit.

A5 asks acceptance for a hold that no longer holds. Its page correction landed at 00:03 inside another session's commit, and the gate now lands green under the existing grant. Do you accept the packet as written, accept the narrower amendment it offers as an alternative of making the snapshot section's counts writable by the loop that checks them, or return it to be re-presented against the state that now exists?

decisions/0050 owns the verification time budget. This witness measured 11.79s three times with the tree quiet, so the packet's residual about failing past 15.000s under load is not reproducible today. Is the budget still the right question, or is it a load artifact to record and leave?
